paras: The St. Joseph exposition grounds riot was an attack on Black people by a crowd of "roughs" at the exposition grounds in St. Joseph, Missouri, on July 4, 1881. The crowd tried to drive all "colored people" off the grounds, fractured one man's skull, beat a youth unconscious and fatally injured an old man named Harris before the military and extra police put down what the report called a riot.

According to a brief report in the Kirksville Weekly Graphic, the crowd was "headed by a cripple named Bruce" and set out to put all colored people off the exposition grounds on the Fourth. Jas. Browning, a Black man, had his skull fractured, and a white man who stepped in to protect him had his jaw broken and suffered other injuries. A Black youth named Fowler was beaten into insensibility.

An old Black man named Harris was struck with a chair and cut with a knife, and he died of his injuries; other Black men were badly hurt. During the riot a little girl was run down by the city marshal and had her leg broken. The military was summoned, and with additional police the riot was quelled.
The report closed by noting "terrible excitement over the affair". No report of arrests, an inquest into Harris's death, or charges against Bruce or others appears in the coverage.

The riot is known from a single paragraph on the front page of the Weekly Graphic of Kirksville, Missouri, published on July 8, 1881, four days after the attack. The item named the attackers as "roughs", stated that their aim was to remove colored people from the grounds, and listed the injuries without editorial comment. It gave no county, no time of day, and no names for the white man or the girl who were hurt, and no follow-up appears in the coverage.

accounts.label: News paragraph
accounts.gist: Roughs led by Bruce tried to drive colored people off the exposition grounds, injuring several and killing an old man named Harris, until the military and extra police quelled the riot.

framing.detail: A short news item calling the attackers 'a crowd of roughs' and the event a 'riot', listing the injuries and noting 'terrible excitement', with no editorial comment.

record_check.dossier: The dead man is printed 'Harris' in the re-read text ('Harus' is an OCR variant); the unnamed white man and a little girl were also injured.
Browning, Fowler, Harris and the other injured men are described as colored; the man who interfered was white; the girl's race is not stated.
At least 2 named (Browning, Fowler) plus 'other colored men badly injured'.
A crowd of roughs headed by a cripple named Bruce.
Also cutting with a knife and an attempt to expel all colored people from the grounds.
Not applicable: the victims were attendees at the grounds, not in custody or sought.
The county is not named in the coverage.
